justification: Display-string rename across four marketing surfaces: the brief page H1/CTA and its metadata titles become Site Report, the how-it-works listing follows, and the homepage workbench band renames Verify to Site Controls. Companion to the info-site rename (lmcdo/website PR 13) so both surfaces present the same product names. No routes, data paths, engine logic, or subdomains change.

pre_impl.existing_data: The naming decision comes from this session's grounded naming study (credit File/Report/Score, NSW conveyancing vernacular): Site Report / Topic Reports / Site Controls, with Verify retired as a tier label because it is a verb and sits on the internal banned-language list. The info-site half of the rename is already merged as lmcdo/website PR 13.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Verified before editing that the strings targeted are display copy only: the intelligence-brief route path, Trigger.dev task names, API routes, and the verify. subdomain host-routing are untouched, so nothing that machines match on changes.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new capability and no new components: pure string replacement inside four existing files. Deliberately NOT renamed: the in-app Verify workbench chrome under /assessment (a larger follow-up), code identifiers, PostHog event names, and blog articles which are historical artifacts.

functions: N/A - display-string replacements only; no function added, changed, or removed.
values: N/A - no DB or API values involved; static JSX strings and metadata titles only.
queries: N/A - no database access in this change.

break_it.scenario: Search engines and existing backlinks lose ranking continuity because the page metadata titles changed from Intelligence Brief to Site Report.
break_it.what_happens: SERP entries re-index under the new title and searches for the old name stop matching the page title.
break_it.how: URLs and routes are unchanged so all backlinks still resolve; the OG description retains the descriptive planning keywords; the old name survives on the info site engine sheet as a formerly-the-Intelligence-Brief recognition line during transition.
break_it.repro: Fetch /reports/intelligence-brief after deploy and view source: the title tag reads Site Report while the URL and canonical are unchanged.

break_it.scenario: A returning user who knows the product as the Intelligence Brief lands on the renamed page and thinks they are in the wrong product.
break_it.what_happens: Confusion or abandonment at the moment of arrival on the brief page.
break_it.how: The route, layout, content, and generate flow are pixel-identical apart from the name; the plotdetect.com.au engine sheet that links here carries a formerly-the-Intelligence-Brief line, so the arriving user has just read the mapping.
break_it.repro: Follow the Site Report tier card from the plotdetect homepage to the renamed page and confirm the recognition line precedes the transition.

break_it.scenario: A missed occurrence leaves mixed naming on one surface, e.g. the H1 says Site Report while a button still says Generate Intelligence Brief.
break_it.what_happens: The page contradicts itself and undermines the rename it is meant to complete.
break_it.how: Grepped the four marketing surfaces for Intelligence Brief and standalone Verify after patching; remaining hits are a code comment in reports/page.tsx and the in-app workbench chrome, both deliberately out of scope and listed as follow-up.
break_it.repro: Run grep -rn 'Intelligence Brief' over frontend-nextjs/app/reports/intelligence-brief and frontend-nextjs/app/page.tsx; only the provenance.ts internal comment remains.

post_merge.db_reset: Not required - no database or schema changes.
post_merge.secrets: No secrets involved - display copy only.
post_merge.other_repo: Pairs with lmcdo/website PR 13 (info-site rename); each deploys independently but the naming is only consistent once both are live.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - on the Vercel preview: /reports/intelligence-brief H1 and generate button read Site Report, the tab title reads Site Report, the homepage workbench band reads Site Controls, and /how-it-works lists Site Report.
